exposure: Mode of delivery (cesarean section vs. vaginal)
Infant diet (formula consumption, amount of breast milk consumed)
cohort: The study included 212 3-month-old infants and 99 pregnant women in their third trimester.
finding: Infants consuming any formula had increased overall richness and diversity of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARG), and cesarean-born infants had increased diversity of ARG within their resistomes, including specific increases in aminoglycoside, beta-lactamase, and tetracycline ARG.
mod_finding: Delivery by cesarean section was associated with increased diversity of ARG, and cesarean-born infants had increased richness of aminoglycoside ARG and increased diversity of beta-lactamase and tetracycline ARG relative to vaginally born infants.
cross-section timing: 3 months postpartum (for infants) and third trimester (for pregnant women)
